market.worldSizeUSD_B_range: Aerospace & defense parts manufacturing: $643.31B (2024) to $961.38B by 2032 (5.15%/yr), or $1,003.0B (2025) to $1,426.9B by 2033 (5.4%/yr). Global UAV market: $26.12B (2025) to $40.56B by 2030 (9.2%/yr), or $32B (2024) to $63.1B by 2030 (12%/yr). Commercial drone market: $30.02B (2024) to $54.64B by 2030 (10.6%/yr).
globalCompetitors: Rolls-Royce, GE Aviation, Honeywell, Boeing, Safran, Collins Aerospace as OEM customers (not competitors) — the primary competitive comparison is against other Indian precision-component makers, see peers[]
market.domesticSlice: India drone market: $654M (2024) to $1,437M by 2029 (17.0%/yr) — faster-growing than the global UAV rate. India's Union Budget 2024-25 allocated ~$68.3B to defense including ~$20.8B capital outlay.

structureFacts: Government drone-sector policy push: PLI scheme for drones, 'Drone Shakti' initiative, liberalized Drone Rules 2021; GST cut to 5% on commercial drones and abolished on military drones/critical defence equipment
DRDO allocated ~$4B in 2024 for drone-system development
Defence Ministry reportedly executing its largest-ever indigenous drone procurement program, splitting orders across multiple domestic manufacturers to build parallel production lines

adoptionStructure.note: Order flow is driven by defense capital-outlay budgets, indigenization/Make-in-India mandates, and specific program wins rather than open-market demand — not a repurchase-rate category
